For commercial re-use, please contact journals.permissions@oup.com Abstract Objective To examine disease and target engagement biomarkers in the RISE-SSc trial of riociguat in early diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis and their potential to predict the response to treatment. Methods Patients were randomized to riociguat ( n = 60) or placebo ( n = 61) for 52 weeks. Skin biopsies and plasma/serum samples were obtained at baseline and week 14. Plasma cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP) was assessed using radio-immunoassay. α-Smooth muscle actin (αSMA) and skin thickness were determined by immunohistochemistry, mRNA markers of fibrosis by qRT-PCR in skin biopsies, and serum CXC motif chemokine ligand 4 (CXCL-4) and soluble platelet endothelial cell adhesion molecule-1 (sPECAM-1) by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Results By week 14, cGMP increased by 94 (78)% with riociguat and 10 (39)% with placebo ( P < 0.001, riociguat vs placebo). Serum sPECAM-1 and CXCL-4 decreased with riociguat vs placebo ( P = 0.004 and P = 0.008, respectively). There were no differences in skin collagen markers between the two groups. Higher baseline serum sPECAM-1 or the detection of αSMA-positive cells in baseline skin biopsies was associated with a larger reduction of modified Rodnan skin score from baseline at week 52 with riociguat vs placebo (interaction P -values 0.004 and 0.02, respectively). Conclusion Plasma cGMP increased with riociguat, suggesting engagement with the nitric oxide–soluble guanylate cyclase–cGMP pathway. Riociguat was associated with a significant reduction in sPECAM-1 (an angiogenic biomarker) vs placebo. Elevated sPECAM-1 and the presence of αSMA-positive skin cells may help to identify patients who could benefit from riociguat in terms of skin fibrosis. Introduction Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a severe and debilitating autoimmune connective tissue disease. It is characterized by fibrosis, inflammation, microvascular injury and systemic organ manifestations including pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), interstitial lung disease, renal dysfunction and failure, diffuse gastrointestinal disease, and myocardial involvement [ 1–4 ]. The nitric oxide (NO)–soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC)–cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP) pathway plays an important role in tissue homeostasis through various mechanisms including antifibrotic and anti-inflammatory effects [ 5 , 6 ]. In preclinical in vitro and in vivo studies, the soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator riociguat exhibited anti-inflammatory, antifibrotic and antiproliferative effects mediated partly by the attenuation of TGF-β signalling [ 5–7 ]. The phase 3 PATENT trial of riociguat in PAH [ 8 , 9 ] included a subgroup with PAH associated with SSc, in whom riociguat prevented the decline in functional capacity and was well tolerated [ 10 ]. In addition, riociguat improved digital blood flow in some patients with Raynaud’s phenomenon in a single-dose pilot study [ 11 ]. These observations suggested that riociguat may reduce tissue fibrosis in SSc, and led to the investigation of riociguat in the phase 2b RIociguat Safety and Efficacy in patients with early diffuse cutaneous Systemic Sclerosis (RISE-SSc) study [ 12 ]. Treatment with riociguat for 52 weeks did not significantly improve the primary end point (modified Rodnan skin score [mRSS]) vs placebo; however, a numerical decrease in mRSS was seen with riociguat ( P = 0.08 vs placebo) and analyses of secondary and exploratory endpoints showed potential efficacy [ 12 ]. Prognostic biomarkers help to identify patients who are at high risk for certain disease outcomes, such as organ involvement or death in patients with diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (dcSSc), irrespective of treatment. Predictive biomarkers allow physicians to predict response to treatment [ 13 ]. Both types of biomarkers may help to inform clinical decision-making and efforts have been made to identify predictive parameters for disease progression in dcSSc [ 14–16 ]. Target engagement biomarkers confirm delivery of the drug and indicate that it is acting on its target. This report describes the pre-specified exploratory biomarker analysis from RISE-SSc. The objectives were to examine the effects of riociguat on its target pharmacological pathway, to investigate the prognostic value of biomarkers in the placebo group (who did not receive targeted treatments for SSc other than rescue therapy at investigator discretion from week 26), and to investigate whether biomarkers could predict the effects of riociguat on skin fibrosis, measures of disease activity and progression of lung disease.

molecular_mechanism_and_relationship.activity_type_context: Riociguat treatment in early diffuse cutaneous Systemic Sclerosis (SSc) and its pathogenesis.
molecular_mechanism_and_relationship.mechanism_description: Riociguat, a soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator, acts by activating the nitric oxide–soluble guanylate cyclase–cGMP pathway, thereby elevating plasma cGMP levels. This pathway is crucial for tissue homeostasis, exerting antifibrotic and anti-inflammatory effects, and compensates for low NO levels observed in injured endothelial cells in SSc. Riociguat also exhibits antifibrotic properties partly by attenuating TGF-β/TGF-β1 signalling, a key mediator of fibrotic processes that promotes mesenchymal differentiation and αSMA expression in SSc. Beyond its direct target engagement (cGMP), riociguat reduces inflammatory markers such as sPECAM-1, which is involved in leukocyte transmigration and whose elevation may reflect a compensatory response associated with skin fibrosis progression. Riociguat also reduces CXCL-4, a chemokine that mediates fibrosis by transforming cells into myofibroblasts and promoting collagen production, suggesting a benefit for peripheral vasculopathy. Other related biomarkers like ADMA and SDMA (NO inhibitors), ERK (involved in tissue fibrosis), and VASP (cGMP-dependent protein kinase substrate) are part of the broader mechanistic landscape in SSc.
related_biomarkers: Soluble platelet endothelial cell adhesion molecule-1 (sPECAM-1)

dose_intensity_and_specificity.dose_comparison_summary: The study primarily compared riociguat to placebo. A concentration-dependent effect of riociguat on cGMP was observed, with cGMP levels correlating with riociguat pharmacokinetic parameters (AUC: r = 0.489, P = 0.001; Cmax: r = 0.485, P = 0.008; Ctrough: r = 0.496, P = 0.001). Furthermore, riociguat's effect on mRSS reduction was more pronounced in αSMA-positive patients with higher baseline mRSS (17–22 units) compared to those with lower baseline mRSS (10 to <17 units).
dose_intensity_and_specificity.specificity_finding: Riociguat demonstrated specificity by increasing cGMP levels, engaging the NO–sGC–cGMP pathway, and reducing inflammatory markers sPECAM-1 and CXCL-4, while other biomarkers remained largely unchanged. Importantly, higher baseline serum sPECAM-1 or the presence of αSMA-positive cells in skin biopsies predicted a larger reduction in modified Rodnan skin score with riociguat (interaction P-values 0.004 and 0.02, respectively). The predictive effect of αSMA-positive cells for mRSS reduction with riociguat was further specific to patients who were also positive for anti-RNA polymerase III or anti-Scl-70 antibodies (interaction P = 0.005).

clinical_implication_and_population.target_population: Patients with early diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (dcSSc) fulfilling ACR/EULAR classification criteria, specifically those with a modified Rodnan Skin Score (mRSS) of 10–22 units. The findings are particularly relevant for subgroups with elevated baseline serum sPECAM-1, αSMA-positive cells, higher baseline mRSS, and/or positivity for anti-RNA polymerase III or anti-Scl-70 antibodies, as these patients may benefit more from riociguat treatment.
clinical_implication_and_population.health_implication: Riociguat treatment shows potential for modulating anti-inflammatory properties and improving vascular function in SSc patients, as evidenced by increased cGMP and reduced sPECAM-1 and CXCL-4. Crucially, the study identifies a method for predicting treatment response in patients with early diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis, particularly regarding skin fibrosis progression, a severe characteristic of the disease. This offers a way to identify patients most likely to benefit from riociguat.
clinical_implication_and_population.risk_classification: Diagnostic/Prognostic Utility (for SSc progression): Higher baseline sPECAM-1 and αSMA positivity are associated with increased mRSS progression, identifying patients at higher risk. Predictive Utility (for treatment response): Higher baseline sPECAM-1 levels and αSMA positivity, especially in autoantibody-positive subgroups, predict a greater reduction of mRSS with riociguat treatment. Therapeutic/Protective Benefit: Riociguat demonstrates potential therapeutic benefit by reducing mRSS progression in specific patient subgroups and exhibiting anti-inflammatory effects (decreased sPECAM-1 and CXCL-4), indicating a protective role and warranting monitoring of therapeutic response.

biomarker_reliability_and_future_focus.reliability_assessment: The predictive utility of sPECAM-1 and αSMA-positive cells for riociguat treatment response appears promising, with αSMA positivity being consistently associated with clinical endpoints. However, reliability concerns exist: all reported P-values are nominal and exploratory due to the primary endpoint not reaching statistical significance. Outliers were removed for hsCRP and CXCL-4 (with caution advised for CXCL-4 due to potential assay issues). Data for some immunohistochemistry markers, ADMA, SDMA, and αSMA status were incomplete for a few patients. Limitations include the visual analogue scale for αSMA assessment, imputation of values, and the generalizability of results to all SSc patients.
